title: Fabrication of 3D Controlled in vitro Microenvironments
author: Ozdil, Onal, et al.

steps.title: Pre‑heat hot plate
steps.instruction: Set the hot plate to 65 °C at least 30 min before use to ensure uniform heating; place a sheet of aluminum foil on the plate.

steps.title: Prepare wafer and apply SU‑8
steps.instruction: Using tweezers, remove a silicon wafer from its package, place it on the foil‑covered hot plate for ~5 min, then transfer to the bench; pour SU‑8 2075 onto the wafer from a bottle held close to the surface to avoid bubbles.

steps.title: Spread SU‑8 evenly
steps.instruction: Loosely cover the bottle mouth with aluminum foil, let the resin flow back, then gently move the wafer in a circular motion at an angle to spread SU‑8 without bubbles; let the wafer sit on the bench ~10 min to equilibrate to room temperature.

steps.title: Spin‑coat to desired thickness
steps.instruction: Place the wafer on the spin‑coater (inner surface pre‑covered with foil) and use the appropriate recipe; for a final thickness of ~200 µm: ramp to 500 rpm in 5 s, spin 500 rpm 5 s, ramp to 1000 rpm in 5 s, spin 1000 rpm 20 s, ramp down to 500 rpm in 5 s, spin 500 rpm 5 s, ramp down to 0 rpm in 5 s. Wait for the spinner to stop before opening the lid.

steps.title: Soft‑bake SU‑8
steps.instruction: Remove the wafer, place it on aluminum foil on the bench, then put it on the hot plate at 65 °C for 20 min; increase temperature to 95 °C and bake for 5 h (3–4 h is sufficient for thin layers). Dispose of contaminated materials according to institutional guidelines.

steps.title: Verify soft‑bake and pre‑heat for post‑bake
steps.instruction: Set a second hot plate to 95 °C at least 30 min in advance; place the soft‑baked wafer on the plate. If wrinkles appear, let the wafer relax on the bench ~5 min, then return to the hot plate for an additional 10 min bake; repeat until no wrinkles are observed.

steps.title: UV expose SU‑8
steps.instruction: Calculate exposure time from mask‑aligner power (e.g., 8 mW cm⁻²). Use 60 s for ~400 µm thickness or 30 s for <200 µm (over‑expose intentionally). Place the wafer on the aligner stage, position the acetate mask with the opaque side toward the SU‑8, and expose.

steps.title: Post‑exposure bake
steps.instruction: After exposure, let the wafer relax on the bench for 5 min; then bake at 65 °C for 5 min followed by 95 °C for ~15 min. Turn off the hot plate and allow the wafer to cool slowly to room temperature.

steps.title: Develop SU‑8 master
steps.instruction: Equilibrate SU‑8 developer and isopropanol to room temperature. Submerge the wafer in developer in a petri dish for 5 min (no shaking), then shake for 15 min. Discard the developer, add fresh developer and shake for 20 min to remove unexposed SU‑8.

steps.title: Inspect and finish development
steps.instruction: If the pattern contains thin‑layer posts, develop for only 10–15 min and examine under a stereo microscope with a UV filter. Perform an isopropanol test: apply a few drops of IPA; a white precipitate indicates under‑development. If well‑developed, wash the wafer 10× with fresh developer then 10× with IPA, finally dry with dust‑free tissue.

steps.title: Clean SU‑8 master
steps.instruction: Wash petri dishes and tweezers sequentially with acetone, IPA, and deionized water. Handle all subsequent SU‑8 operations under yellow‑light illumination in the clean room.

steps.title: Prepare PDMS mixture
steps.instruction: Weigh Sylgard 184 base and curing agent at a 10:1 ratio (e.g., 27 g base + 3 g curing agent for a total of 30 g for a 4‑inch wafer). Mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Degas PDMS
steps.instruction: Place the mixed PDMS in a vacuum desiccator and degas for two cycles of 10 min each.

steps.title: Clean SU‑8 master before casting
steps.instruction: While PDMS is degassing, wash the SU‑8 master with 70 % ethanol, then with deionized water, and finally with the demolding buffer (Triton‑X‑100:H₂O:EtOH = 1:9:40).

steps.title: Cast PDMS onto master
steps.instruction: In a 10 cm glass petri dish, shape a shallow aluminum foil container, place a piece of double‑sticky tape in the centre, and set the cleaned SU‑8 master inside. Pour the degassed PDMS over the master, level the surface, and let polymerize at room temperature for at least 2 days.

steps.title: Demold PDMS
steps.instruction: After the 2‑day polymerization, gently separate the solid PDMS replica from the SU‑8 master; applying a small amount of ethanol at the interface can aid removal.

steps.title: Clean PDMS molds
steps.instruction: Cut the PDMS replica to size and punch inlet/outlet holes. Remove dust with Scotch tape, then wash with deionized water several times. Sonicate in water for 10 min, rinse 5× with water; sonicate in 70 % ethanol for 5 min, rinse twice with ethanol; keep in 70 % ethanol on the bench for 5 min; rinse once with water in a laminar hood and aspirate excess liquid. After drying, place molds (patterned side up) in an autoclaved petri dish, cover with foil, and let dry at room temperature for 2 days.

steps.title: UV/ozone treat and bond
steps.instruction: Treat a clean glass slide and a PDMS mold in a UV/ozone cleaner for 5 min each. Immediately bring the treated surfaces together and press to bond, forming the 3D CivM device.

steps.title: Heat bonded devices
steps.instruction: Place the bonded devices on a hot plate set to ~100 °C for at least 10 min, covering them with elevated foil pieces to create an oven effect and protect from dust. Turn off the hot plate and allow the devices to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Sterilize 3D CivMs
steps.instruction: Rinse all interior and exterior surfaces with 70 % ethanol in a laminar flow hood, aspirate liquid, then wash the channels twice with autoclaved deionized water. Aspirate again, transfer devices to a new autoclaved petri dish, let dry, expose to UV light for 30 min, then place in an oven at 80 °C for 24 h to restore hydrophobicity.

steps.title: Prepare cell‑laden Matrigel
steps.instruction: Thaw Matrigel (stored at –80 °C) overnight in an ice bath at +4 °C. On ice, mix Matrigel with a cell suspension at a 1:1 volume ratio using a 200 µL pipette; keep the mixture on an aluminum rack in the ice bath (+4 °C).

steps.title: Load hydrogel into channels
steps.instruction: Place the sterilized CivMs on 70 % ethanol‑soaked sterile filter paper on an aluminum block in the ice bath to keep them cold. Load the cell‑laden Matrigel into the appropriate channels with a 200 µL pipette, working slowly and holding the device vertically to prevent gel leakage through pillars. After loading, allow polymerization at room temperature for 30 min, then invert the device to keep cells suspended away from the bottom glass.

steps.title: Add media and incubate
steps.instruction: After gel polymerization, add culture medium to the reservoir ports, seal inlets/outlets with PDMS pieces, place devices in sterile petri dishes with open microcentrifuge tubes of autoclaved water to minimize evaporation, and incubate at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂ (or appropriate cell‑culture conditions).

steps.title: Collect experimental data
steps.instruction: Acquire phase‑contrast or fluorescence images of the cells in the 3D CivMs daily; process images with Photoshop or ImageJ as needed.
